component: Payload, envelope and trust-policy structural schemas
constraints: Offline publisher/consumer tooling: closed portable Draft 2020-12 objects, bounded arrays and strings, exact allowed labels, no runtime dependency or remote schema retrieval.
Runtime remains responsible for byte/depth and lexical bounds, selected-field uniqueness, reference integrity, signatures, trust pins and time. No throughput SLA or target-device qualification.
alternatives: Draft 2020-12 with python-jsonschema and an explicit offline referencing registry; direct calls into the current runtime expose semantic distinctions.
JavaScript/TypeScript Ajv 2020 validator; Java/Kotlin networknt validator as independent standard-schema consumers.
CUE declarations with JSON Schema interchange for constraint authoring; Pydantic strict models for application validation and schema generation.
rationale: KEEP the published JSON Schema contracts and direct Python conformance comparison. Current schemas agree with the reviewed claim vocabulary; migration does not supply missing signature or lexical semantics.

FIX assurance coverage: five independently removed payload const/enum constraints survived all eight previous passport-schema methods. Two new methods cover 27 valid combinations and 12 invalid claims; all five removals now cause assertion failures.
limits: Alternative tools were researched from their official documentation, not executed or benchmarked. No speed, memory or universal language ranking is claimed.

The selected checker tests the published artifact directly and compares actual runtime behavior in process. Generated application models would require additional exact-wire checks and independent artifact validation.
No whole-lane completion, installed-distribution acceptance, physical, real-time, MLS/CNSA or availability qualification.
